intro: The impeccable pass fixed 9 defects on London without changing any words, links or images. Its score went from 13/20 to 15/20. These four would change how the page looks, so each one waits for your yes. Before and after for each: https://claude.ai/artifact/2rfZmgNNYgP7v8rnuRiszN

questions.context: On a phone each is drawn about 319px wide, so its labels come out at 5–7px. Recommended: (a). Why: the infographics are on the page to be read, and right now a phone reader can't. Trade-off: six new image files (cheapest Gemini model where any generation is needed; mostly a re-bake of the same content). They come to you as drafts at the Asset Gate before anything is published.

options.label: Yes, re-draw them for phones and bring them to the Asset Gate
No, keep them as they are

questions.question: D4 · Re-draw the six phone infographics so their labels can be read?

questions.context: From 1024px wide there are tall empty spaces beside long prose. Recommended: (a). Why: it fills the empty space with something useful and changes nothing on a phone. Trade-off: on desktop the heading and photo stay put while the prose scrolls, which some readers notice.
questions.question: D1 · Keep the heading and photo in view beside long chapters on desktop?

questions.context: Recommended: (a). Why: on a phone they currently look lighter than the paragraph under them, so they don't read as headings. Trade-off: none that I can see.
questions.question: D2 · Make the small chapter headings (H4 to H6) bold in brand steel, like the rest of the site?

questions.context: They pass the legal minimum (24px), but they're small for thumbs. Recommended: (a). Why: it's an accessibility gain on every page, with only slightly roomier spacing. Trade-off: it repaints the header, breadcrumb and footer on every built page, so every page's render gate re-runs.
questions.question: D3 · Pad the header, breadcrumb and footer links to a 44px tap size on every page?

title: London Harden pass · four visual changes
